purpose: Section 21: manually classify a deterministic sample of the real 477 review items (regenerated fresh against real Postgres, since the original run's rows were cleaned up) to determine whether the architecture discriminates real material review need from indiscriminate over-flagging, or is only vacuously satisfying NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE.

regeneration.script: scripts/cert-3f1-6-section21-volume-quality-sample.ts (auditor-authored re-run of the exact same real FWRG+LSB loaders/inputs/call-sequence as scripts/phase-3f1-5-r-safe-failure-volume-analysis.ts, with a full per-item JSON dump added before cleanup)
regeneration.note: Exact reproduction of the 477 figure from docs/phase-3f1-5-r-residual-foundation/18-review-event-volume-analysis.json confirms the volume claim was real and is reproducible, not a one-time artifact.

populationDistribution.observation: Only 3 of the 7 possible reasonCodes actually occur in this real population (no INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT, OPERATIVE_STATE_UNCERTAIN, UNSUPPORTED_EXPRESSION, or VERIFICATION_CONTRADICTION events fired against these two real packages) - consistent with FWRG/LSB being credit agreements without cross-package amendment conflicts or IR-inexpressible mechanics, not evidence of a coding gap (Section 20 already independently proved all 7 reasonCode-producing paths work when their triggering condition actually occurs).

sample.method: Stratified deterministic sample: first 7 items by id within COMPILATION_FAILURE, first 7 within MISSING_REQUIRED_SEMANTIC_DIMENSION, all 5 within SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY (the entire rare-but-highest-signal category), plus 3 additional CRITICAL-materiality items not already captured - 22 items total, roughly 4.6% of the population, deliberately weighted toward the smaller/rarer categories to avoid a sample dominated entirely by one repetitive pattern.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'The Borrower shall not... create... any Lien... except:' - the base negative-covenant prohibition itself
classifications.why: The general prohibition statement is the operative core of the whole Liens covenant; confirming it has adequate IR representation (as opposed to only its enumerated exceptions) is a genuinely reasonable thing to want confirmed, even though it is less economically pointed than a dollar-figure basket.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'Liens securing the Secured Obligations' - boilerplate, no dollar figure
classifications.why: Standard boilerplate permitted-lien carve-out (liens securing the facility itself) with no quantifiable capacity at stake; unlikely to be the kind of omission a CFO needs surfaced with the same urgency as a dollar-denominated basket.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'Liens for Taxes which...' - boilerplate, no dollar figure
classifications.why: Same as 6.02(a) - a standard permitted-tax-lien carve-out with no economic magnitude.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: Statutory liens of landlords/carriers/mechanics etc. incurred in ordinary course - boilerplate
classifications.why: Classic 'Permitted Encumbrances' boilerplate carve-out, no dollar figure.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: '...for amounts overdue by more than 60 days and contested in good faith...' - a continuation/proviso of 6.02(c)
classifications.why: Reads as a grammatical continuation of 6.02(c) rather than an independently meaningful claim - source-side over-fragmentation splits one boilerplate exception into two review items.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'Liens granted or arising...' (truncated) - boilerplate
classifications.why: Same pattern as the other 6.02 sub-clauses - boilerplate, no dollar figure.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: Survey exceptions, easements, rights-of-way, zoning restrictions etc. - classic Permitted Encumbrances boilerplate
classifications.why: No dollar figure, no capacity impact - textbook non-economic permitted-lien boilerplate.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'The Borrower shall not... create, incur... any Indebtedness... except:' - the base negative-covenant prohibition
classifications.why: Same reasoning as the 6.02 chapeau - the base prohibition is the operative core of the covenant.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'Indebtedness of...' (truncated) - intercompany-debt basket header, no dollar figure
classifications.why: The wrapper/header for the intercompany-debt permission; unlimited by design in most agreements of this kind, no economic magnitude of its own.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'the Borrower to Holdings and/or any Restricted Subsidiary and/or...' (truncated) - fragment continuing into (ii)
classifications.why: A sentence fragment of the same intercompany-debt basket as 6.01(b) and 6.01(b)(ii) - over-fragmentation of one basket into five separate review items (6.01(b), (b)(i), (b)(ii), (b)(ii)(A), (b)(ii)(B)).

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: 'any Restricted Subsidiary to Holdings...; provided that...' (truncated) - fragment continuing into (ii)(A)/(ii)(B)
classifications.why: Same fragmentation pattern as 6.01(b)(i).

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: A genuine cross-referenced condition: intercompany debt to a non-Loan-Party subsidiary is conditioned on the related Investment being permitted under Section 6.06
classifications.why: This is a real substantive interlock between two covenant families (Indebtedness and Investments) that a compiler could easily miss representing - genuinely worth a human confirming.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: Guaranties/letters of credit/surety bonds securing performance in the ordinary course - boilerplate, no dollar cap
classifications.why: Standard operational-guarantee carve-out, no economic magnitude.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $2,500,000 guaranty basket - 'no rule is anchored to this unit's exact citation, but its numeric value 2500000 appears elsewhere in the covering candidate(s)' compiled IR - review required to confirm this is the same economic figure, not a coincidental match'
classifications.why: A precise, well-targeted, genuinely uncertain question about whether a specific dollar figure was correctly attributed - exactly the kind of question a human reviewer can resolve quickly and that matters if wrong.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $21,000,000 / 35% EBITDA Restricted Payments basket, same numeric-match-uncertainty pattern
classifications.why: Same reasoning as 6.01(g)(i) - a real, large-dollar basket with genuine attribution uncertainty.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: Same $21,000,000 figure, a related carryforward provision
classifications.why: Same reasoning - likely related to 6.04(a)(x) (a builder-basket carryforward of the same cap), still a genuinely useful confirmation to request.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $70,000,000 / 5.5% of consolidated assets basket, same pattern
classifications.why: Large, specific dollar basket with genuine numeric-attribution uncertainty - high-value review target.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $500,000 basket, same pattern
classifications.why: Smaller dollar figure than the other SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY items but still a specific, real basket with genuine attribution uncertainty.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $5,000,000 existing-indebtedness Schedule 6.01 threshold, no IR representation found at all
classifications.why: A real dollar threshold with zero compiled representation - a genuinely consequential gap, correctly flagged at CRITICAL tier.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $30,000,000 / 50% EBITDA non-Loan-Party-subsidiary debt basket, no IR representation found
classifications.why: A large, real basket entirely absent from compiled IR - exactly the kind of omission this architecture exists to catch.

classifications.sourceEvidenceSummary: $30,000,000 / 50% EBITDA capital-lease/purchase-money basket, no IR representation found
classifications.why: Same reasoning as 6.01(j) - a real, large, unrepresented basket.

interpretation.reasoning: The population is NOT flagged indiscriminately. There is a clear, legible quality gradient visible even without any explicit priority field: every one of the 5 SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY items (a rare category - only 5 of 477) and every CRITICAL-materiality MISSING_REQUIRED_SEMANTIC_DIMENSION item sampled describes a specific, real, economically consequential dollar basket with a genuine, well-articulated reason a human should look at it (either a numeric-match ambiguity or total absence of compiled representation for a large basket). These 8 items are unambiguously TRUE_MATERIAL_REVIEW_NEED and none was a FALSE_REVIEW_EVENT anywhere in the sample - the architecture never manufactured a review need where none existed. At the same time, roughly 36% of this sample (8/22, concentrated entirely in the boilerplate enumerated-exception sub-clauses of 6.01/6.02) carries little independent analytical value: standard permitted-lien and permitted-guaranty carve-outs with no dollar figure, each nonetheless becoming its own full-weight OPEN_REVIEW item indistinguishable in status/urgency from a $30,000,000 basket gap. A further ~14% (3/22) reflects source-side over-fragmentation - one basket's multi-clause definition split into several review items rather than one.
interpretation.rootCauseOfTheNoiseFraction: The materiality gate (derive.ts's MATERIAL_TIERS check) is binary (CRITICAL/MATERIAL vs. REVIEW_UNCERTAIN/INFORMATIONAL) and inherited unchanged from semantic-coverage's own upstream materiality classification - it does not further weight by economic magnitude (a $500,000 basket and a boilerplate carve-out with no dollar figure at all can both land at MATERIAL tier). This is a pre-existing semantic-coverage characteristic, not something the safe-failure module itself introduced or could reasonably be expected to fix (per this phase's own derive.ts documentation: it 'introduces zero new semantic judgment' and defers entirely to the upstream coverage classification).

verdictStatement: NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE is satisfied with REAL, not vacuous, signal in this sample - a majority of sampled items (14/22, 64%) carry genuine or plausible material review justification, and zero sampled items were flatly wrong (FALSE_REVIEW_EVENT). The architecture does not indiscriminately flag everything with no discriminating signal, so this does NOT rise to the charter's 'vacuous satisfaction' failure mode. However, a meaningful minority (~36%) of the sample is low-value boilerplate-carve-out noise indistinguishable in status/priority from the highest-value items, plus some source-side over-fragmentation of single baskets into multiple review items. This is a genuine signal-quality concern worth a human reviewer's attention at scale (477 items with no priority ranking would present a real triage burden), rated MINOR rather than MAJOR_NON_BLOCKING because: (a) it is a pre-existing property of the upstream materiality classification the safe-failure module correctly and deliberately does not re-judge, (b) it does not cause any FALSE negative or FALSE positive, only a triage-burden cost, and (c) the highest-value category (SEMANTIC_AMBIGUITY, numeric-attribution uncertainty) is unambiguously well-targeted and the rarest, suggesting the underlying reconciliation logic IS capable of real discrimination when the coverage state itself is more specific.
